decisions.summary: Routine check: no dispute on file, so I took no action and made no refunds or escalations.

Routine check, no action. No agent is blocked: sourcing's 0.03 cap covers both stock-check providers (Stockline 0.02, Ridgeline 0.03), which leaves a margin on the 0.05 query price. There are no earnings to sweep, no invoice to plan and nothing waiting for the CFO.

Routine check: both Stockline and Ridgeline are unreachable (0 paid/0 refused/0 unavailable in last 20 tries). I switched the buy policy to cache-only (supplier none, cache up to 300s) so queries are served from cache and uncached ones are refused without charging customers. No purchases made; budget and mandate unchanged.

Reversed my earlier cache-only policy: the market shows Stockline available at 0.02 with 5 s data and a 0.03 margin (the "unreachable" reading was based on empty history). Set the buy policy to Stockline, max 0.03 per check, 60 s cache. Ridgeline is worse (0.03 price, 15 min old data, 0.02 margin) so it is not used.

Stockline raised its price to 0.06 per check, above our 0.05 sale price and 0.03 mandate cap, so I paused purchases: policy set to supplier none with a 60 s cache, meaning customers get cached checks up to 60 s old and uncached queries are refused without charge. Ridgeline (0.02, but 15-min-old data) was not used since that data is too stale to sell as fresh. No spend made; budget stays at 9.98 and I informed Treasury.

No rebalance yet. Stockline's 0.06 price is above our 0.05 query price, but Ridgeline at 0.02 fits sourcing's 0.03 cap with margin. No customer has been turned away and code shows no agent blocked. I told Sourcing to use Ridgeline where 15-minute-old data is good enough, and to report any turned-away customers so I can design a rebalance. I didn't sweep the 0.18 because it's too small to be worth it now.

Left purchases paused. Stockline at 0.06 is a loss against the 0.05 query price and 0.03 cap. Ridgeline at 0.02 fits the cap, but its data is 15 min old, which I won't sell as fresh stock data without Treasury's approval. Policy stays at supplier none with a 60 s cache, so uncached queries are refused without charge. Spend 0, budget 9.98. Treasury has been asked to decide on Ridgeline use or a query-price change.

No change this wake. Stockline is at 0.06 per check, a loss against our 0.05 sale price and 0.03 cap, and Ridgeline's 15-min-old data is not sellable as fresh without Treasury approval. Buy policy stays at supplier none with a 60 s cache, so queries are served from cache and uncached ones are refused without charge. Spend 0, budget 9.98 left; awaiting Treasury's decision on Ridgeline use or a query-price change.

I didn't approve selling 15-min-old data as a stock check. Freshness is a product and honesty decision, not a treasury one, so Sourcing keeps refusing uncached queries at no charge for now. A rebalance isn't needed yet: no agent is blocked, and Stockline at 0.06 would need a higher query price, not just a higher cap. I didn't sweep the 0.18 because it's too small.

No change. Stockline is at 0.06 per check, a loss against our 0.05 sale price and 0.03 cap, and Ridgeline's 15-min-old data can't be sold as fresh without Treasury's approval, which Treasury has declined for now. The buy policy stays at supplier none with a 60 s cache, so cached checks are served and uncached queries are refused without charge. Spend is 0 and budget is 9.98. Waiting on Treasury's decision on a query-price change or a labelled Ridgeline offer.

Code now shows Sourcing is blocked by its 0.03 cap (3 customers turned away), so I sent the CFO a rebalance as P-0002/P-0003. It would move 2.00 from Treasury to Sourcing and raise Sourcing's cap to 0.06; the total stays at 20.00. I recommended a 0.08 query price (option B) for a 0.02 margin over Stockline. I didn't sweep the 0.18 because it's too small.

No change. Market is unchanged: Stockline is at 0.06 per check (a loss against our 0.05 sale price and 0.03 cap), and Ridgeline's 15-minute-old data can't be sold as fresh without Treasury approval. The buy policy stays at supplier none with a 60 s cache, so cached checks are served and uncached queries are refused without charge. Spend is 0 and budget is 9.98. I'm waiting on the CFO's decision on the Treasury rebalance (cap 0.06, budget 12.00, query price 0.07 or 0.08) before buying again.

Market unchanged: Stockline is at 0.06 per check, a loss against our 0.05 sale price and 0.03 cap, and Ridgeline's 15-min-old data is not sellable as fresh without Treasury approval. Policy stays at supplier none with a 60 s cache, so cached checks are served and uncached queries are refused without charge. Spend 0, budget 9.98 left. Waiting on the CFO's decision on the Treasury rebalance before buying again.
No dispute on file. The only new event is a mandate replacement (P-0003), which is information and needs nothing from me. I took no action, made no refunds, and escalated nothing.

Query price is now 0.08 (mandate P-0003), so my earlier pause based on a 0.05 price was stale. Set the buy policy to Stockline with max 0.06 per check and a 60 s cache: 0.02 margin on 5-second-old data. Ridgeline stays unused because its data is 15 minutes old.

Confirmed the buy policy is Stockline at up to 0.06 per check with a 60 s cache. That gives a 0.02 margin at the 0.08 query price, within the P-0003 cap and the 11.98 budget. Ridgeline stays unused because its data is 15 minutes old. Told Treasury nothing blocks fresh stock checks now.

P-0003 is live (Sourcing cap 0.06, budget 12.00, query price 0.08, total 20.00), so no agent is blocked and every query keeps a margin of at least 0.02. I told Sourcing it can now use Stockline for fresh data. No sweep (0.18 is too small), no invoice, nothing pending for the CFO.

No action. P-0003 is live and the total is 20.00. Sourcing confirmed that Stockline at 0.06 fits its 0.06 cap and leaves a 0.02 margin on the 0.08 query price, and no agent is blocked. The 0.18 net earnings are still too small to sweep, no invoice needs planning and nothing waits for the CFO.

I planned Stockline's EUR 240.00 November licence invoice (SLL-2026-11, due 15 Nov) as P-0004. It pays by SWIFT with fees capped at EUR 20.00. No FX is needed because free euros cover it. P-0004 expires 17:37 UTC and needs the CFO's Face ID. I didn't sweep the 0.44 net earnings because it's still too small, and no agent is blocked.

No change. Query price is 0.08, Stockline sells fresh 5-second-old checks at 0.06 (0.02 margin, above the 0.01 minimum) within my 0.06 cap, and the policy stays at Stockline up to 0.06 with a 60 s cache. Ridgeline stays unused because its data is 15 minutes old. Budget left is 11.86. The Packwise card decline concerns software, not stock checks, so I'm not acting on it now.

The day's sales settled, so I swept 0.70 of net earnings to Airwallex. That is 0.08 more than the 0.62 in event #9, from one more sale. The transfer reached finality and is booked as an Airwallex deposit, but that deposit is simulated: the sandbox can't receive stablecoins. The business account still holds 20.00, enough for the 15.86 the other mandates may still spend, and no agent is blocked, so no rebalance is needed.

I took no action. The 1240.00 EUR payment from Alpenweg Sport AG covers invoice NW-R-201 in full, and code has already matched it to that invoice. Nothing is in suspense, no invoices are open and nothing waits for the CFO. The 0.02 in net earnings is too small to sweep, and no agent is blocked, so no rebalance is needed.

No change. Market is unchanged: Stockline sells 5-second-old checks at 0.06 (0.02 margin at the 0.08 query price), within my 0.06 cap, and the buy policy stays at Stockline up to 0.06 with a 60 s cache. Ridgeline stays unused because its data is 15 minutes old. I'm declining Ridgeline's November regional demand report (0.20 test USD or 15.00 EUR), since it doesn't help stock-check sales and would spend budget with no clear return. Budget left is 11.80 per the market view.
